sovereign_country.strategic_role: 非洲第一大金融枢纽、辐射南部非洲关税同盟（SACU）商贸

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Oversized Furniture and Home Decor

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Agreement
SADC Free Trade Area (Protocol on Trade)
South Africa–United Kingdom Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA), as amended by the General Laws (Anti-Money Laundering and Combatting Terrorism Financing) Amendment Act 22 of 2022; Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended; Companies (Beneficial Ownership Information) Regulations, 2023 (CIPC Notice No. 3479 of 2023); Financial Sector Regulation Act 9 of 2017 (in so far as applicable)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarised copy of passport and identity document of each director and each Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or Home Affairs of the respective country of domicile, with notarial attestation by a local notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (competent authority in the country of origin, South Africa being a contracting party since 30 April 1995)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn Declaration of Beneficial Ownership (prescribed CIPC form CoR 21.1 read with Companies Regulations 2023)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: South African Police Service (SAPS) Commissioner of Oaths, or any domestic Notary Public in the Republic of South Africa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic sworn declaration executed within South Africa; no apostille or consular legalization required if signed in the Republic

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of registered office lease or proof of physical address (for service of process)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registered accommodation/registered office service provider or independent South African attorney; where issued by a foreign public authority, the foreign authority of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if a foreign public document; any consular legalization if apostille not available in the issuing country

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and authorised signatories against the FIC targeted financial sanctions lists (transposing UNSC Resolutions), the OFAC SDN list as a supplementary best-practice measure, the South African Anti-Money Laundering Integrity List (domestic CIPC disqualified persons register), and PEP classification in accordance with FICA section 1 and FIC Public Compliance Communication 4 (PCC 4); enhanced due diligence is triggered for any domestic or foreign prominent public official.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: CIPC e-Services Company Name Reservation Portal (https://eservices.cipc.co.za)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in any of South Africa's 11 official languages, but the CIPC electronic system accepts only Latin-script characters; where the proposed name originates from a non-Latin script, the applicant must furnish an exact English or Afrikaans transliteration and a sworn explanation of the meaning of the name, complying with section 11(1) of the Companies Act 71 of 2008.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a rejection notice issued by CIPC, the applicant may file an administrative objection under Companies Regulation 9 and section 11(4) of the Companies Act within 20 business days of the rejection date, through the CIPC e-Services Objections channel, using Form CoR 9.1 and paying the prescribed objection fee; CIPC must decide the objection within 10 business days, after which a further appeal may be lodged in the High Court of South Africa.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible only where the registered office provider maintains and discloses a physical South African street address at which legal process may be served; a pure virtual or PO Box address without a physical facility does not satisfy section 23(3) of the Companies Act. For an online oversized-furniture e-commerce enterprise, a virtual office combined with an operational warehouse/freight-forwarding address is compliant and commercially standard.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 5% annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection, assessed on the basis that the entity is a low-risk internet retail business with no physical retail premises, no statutory licence, and no significant AML/CFT risk tier; CIPC may verify the registered office in response to a complaint, and SARS may perform random VAT/fiscal verification visits.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: CIPC name search and reservation fee (three name proposals)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per CIPC Fee Schedule 2024/25

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company incorporation filing fee for Proprietary Limited (Pty) Ltd
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per CIPC Fee Schedule 2024/25

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Beneficial Ownership Information filing fee (initial declaration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per CIPC Beneficial Ownership Filing Fee Schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / accommodation address service (one year)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for low-risk non-resident entities with physical address and process-service facility

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarisation and apostille of UBO/director identity documents (two individuals)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public and competent apostille authority in the country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark; in South Africa, per Attorneys Act 53 of 1979 and Notarial Fees Regulations

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/KYC UBO piercing and sanctions/PEP screening (external compliance support)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Independent compliance consultant or law firm
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark per FIC compliance outsourcing rate card

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence retainership and drafting of incorporation documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark, flat retainer based on scope: memorandum of incorporation, first directors’ consents, initial regulatory filings, and legal opinion

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, ss 11 (company names), 14 (incorporation), 15 (Memorandum of Incorporation), 19 (legal personality), 23 (registered office), and 66-72 (board of directors).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) under the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up or issued capital applies to a Proprietary Limited Company. Shares have no par value; the subscriber must deliver the agreed consideration under section 38/40 of the Companies Act, and no escrow account or statutory deposit is prescribed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION
Resolved, by unanimous written consent of the incorporators and the first director of [Company Name] (Pty) Ltd, under Companies Act 71 of 2008 and the Memorandum of Incorporation:

1. Share subscription: The allotment and issue of the initial ordinary shares, and the receipt and sufficiency of the consideration subscribed by the founding shareholders, are approved.
2. Registered office: The registered office and postal address set out in the Notice of Incorporation, being a physical address in South Africa, are adopted for statutory service of process.
3. Officers: The appointment of the sole director, together with the director's authority and banking signing powers, is ratified with effect from incorporation.

This resolution is effective upon adoption.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve the company name with CIPC
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to CIPC e-Services and submit a name reservation application on Form CoR 9.1. Select the private company type, propose a unique name ending with '(Pty) Ltd', and pay the reservation fee. The name is checked for conflicts with existing companies and trademarks before approval.
required_dossiers: Certified identity document or passport of each director/incorporator
Completed Form CoR 9.1 name reservation application
Proof of name reservation fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If queried, respond to CIPC within 10 business days with alternative names or a name variation letter; if refused due to conflict, submit a fresh reservation or lodge an objection with the Companies Tribunal under the Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare the Memorandum of Incorporation and Notice of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company formation practitioner / CIPC standard documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the MOI using the CIPC standard template or a bespoke form, ensuring it addresses share capital, director powers, voting rights, and any restrictions on non-resident ownership. Complete Form CoR 14.1 with the reserved company name, registered physical address, postal address, financial year-end, and first directors. Obtain written consent from each first director to serve.
required_dossiers: Completed Form CoR 14.1 Notice of Incorporation
Registered office consent from the property owner or landlord
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CIPC query identifies inconsistencies, amend the relevant clause or field and re-upload; a standard (Pty) Ltd MOI does not require notarial attestation unless it imposes non-standard statutory restrictions.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodge incorporation documents and pay CIPC registration fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the CoR 14.1 Notice of Incorporation and the MOI electronically through CIPC e-Services or at a CIPC office. Pay the applicable incorporation fee. CIPC will issue a Notice of Registration with a company registration number, and the company acquires separate legal personality on the date stated therein.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If rejected for incomplete data, correct the defect and resubmit without paying another name reservation fee; if formally refused, lodge a reconsideration request with CIPC or apply to the Companies Tribunal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the CIPC registration notice, create an eFiling profile and register for income tax within 21 business days of incorporation. If taxable turnover exceeds ZAR 1 million in any rolling 12-month period, register for VAT. If employees will be appointed, register simultaneously for PAYE, UIF, and Skills Development Levy, and obtain an employer tax reference number.
required_dossiers: Registered bank account details if applying for VAT
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS issues a query or provisional registration, respond through eFiling within the stated deadline and provide certified copies of the requested documents; late or missing responses may result in penalties, which can be remitted only with a sworn statement and supporting evidence.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File beneficial ownership particulars and maintain statutory registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC beneficial ownership filings and company records
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Declare beneficial owners in the CIPC beneficial ownership register within 5 business days of incorporation or any change, and maintain the company's internal beneficial ownership register. Also prepare the register of shareholders, register of directors, minute book, and record the adopted first board resolution and registered office details.
required_dossiers: List of beneficial owners and their percentage interests
Certified identity documents and residential addresses of beneficial owners
CIPC beneficial ownership filing fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is queried, supply the missing particulars or acceptable proof of the date of change within 5 business days; failure to maintain the register may attract a compliance notice, remedied by immediate filing and payment of any prescribed fine.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open the company bank account and issue share certificates
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank under the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Take the certified company registration documents, MOI, and beneficial ownership declaration to a commercial bank to open the corporate account. Provide bank-compliant account-opening resolutions in line with the first board resolution. After the cash or in-kind contribution is received, issue share certificates and record them in the share register.
required_dossiers: First board resolution and director appointment record
Certified IDs and proof of residential address for directors and shareholders
FICA KYC forms and transactional profile
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects KYC documents, resubmit updated or notarially certified identity and address documents; if unresolved, approach another regulated bank or the Ombudsman for Banking Services.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No dedicated industrial licensing board applies to online retail under ISIC 4791; local municipal building control, fire, and environmental health departments are the competent authorities for physical premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sector-specific operating licence is mandated for online retail of oversized furniture. Where a physical warehouse, showroom, or distribution centre is used, the required permission is municipal building plan approval, a Certificate of Occupancy under the National Building Regulations, and, if the business is scheduled under provincial law, a municipal trading licence under the Business Act 71 of 1991.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE); environmental compliance is delegated to provincial and local municipal environmental health authorities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from mandatory EIA for pure online retail and non-hazardous furniture warehousing, unless the development triggers a listed activity under the NEMA EIA Regulations 2014 (e.g. a warehouse/distribution floor area above 2,000 m², vegetation clearance above 1 ha, or location within a sensitive area), in which case either a Basic Assessment or full Scoping and EIA is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No significant industrial effluent is expected; domestic wastewater must comply with municipal sewer by-laws and discharge standards under the National Water Act 36 of 1998. No coating, spraying, or wood-treatment operation is anticipated; any incidental activity using more than 5 tonnes per year of solvent or VOC-emitting material will constitute a listed activity under the National Environmental Management: Air Quality Act 39 of 2004 and require an atmospheric emission licence with applicable emission limits. General non-hazardous waste must be removed by a registered municipal or private waste service; any hazardous waste such as paints, thinners, or adhesives must be consigned and disposed of at a licensed facility under the Waste Act 59 of 2008.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local Fire and Rescue Service, structural load inspection by a registered professional engineer, approved building plans, and workplace clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993, including an electrical certificate of compliance for leased premises, are required before occupying a warehouse, showroom, or office facility.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — eFiling portal (www.sarsefiling.co.za)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-incorporated entity or a South African private company (Pty) Ltd acting as an agent or registered branch must apply for an income tax reference number through SARS eFiling or by lodging form IT100 (Application for Registration for Income Tax) and relevant supporting documents, including the certificate of incorporation, memorandum of incorporation, foreign entity registration proof, and a SARS-appointed representative detail. VAT registration is obtained separately through SARS eFiling under the VAT 101 form. Effective date of VAT registration is aligned to the earlier of commencement of taxable activity or the due date for the first VAT return.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election is available under South African law; the (Pty) Ltd is automatically taxed as a separate legal person at the entity level. Available elections include the election to form a VAT grouping with controlled group entities where turnover thresholds and common control conditions are satisfied, the deemed dividend election for the equity mechanism within hybrid mismatch provisions, and the election to treat the sale of residential units as zero-rated where the buyer is a VAT vendor under the VAT Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: R1,000,000 turnover per annum for compulsory registration (voluntary registration permitted from R50,000 per annum)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: SARS has implemented an electronic e-invoicing framework (SAPICS-compliant tax invoice standards) but real-time fiscal clearance, API-based digital stamping, and block-chain anchored clearance are not currently mandatory for all VAT vendors. VAT returns must be submitted electronically via SARS eFiling; selected high-risk vendors are subject to real-time digital tax invoice reporting through the SARS eInvoicing platform, which requires API integration and digital signature verification for tax invoice authenticity.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods: zero-rating applies under section 11(1)(a) of the VAT Act in respect of supplies of movable goods that are supplied in the course of an export consignment where the goods are delivered to an address in a foreign export country or are removed from South Africa under an approved customs customs manifest, and the supplier retains the prescribed documentary proof. For services: zero-rating applies under section 11(2)(l) and 11(2)(m) where the services are supplied to a non-resident recipient, the recipient is resident outside South Africa, and the services are not in respect of land or movable goods situated in South Africa at the time of supply, and certain labour or intellectual property conditions are satisfied.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / Road Consignment Note
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or bank proof of foreign currency receipt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS may raise additional VAT with interest and a penalty of up to 200% of the tax payable for false or improper zero-rating claims or failure to retain export proof. Deliberate tax evasion or fraud attracts criminal liability under the Tax Administration Act, including imprisonment. Substantiated misrepresentations in export VAT refund claims trigger the VAT clawback provisions under section 44 of the VAT Act, requiring repayment to SARS before any refund accrues; directors of the (Pty) Ltd may be personally liable in respect of the representative's liability under section 62 of the Tax Administration Act if the company defaults on such obligations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB) acting through its Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), which exercises delegated powers of the Minister of Finance under the Currency and Exchanges Act, 1933 (Act No. 9 of 1933) and the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961. Commercial banks operate as SARB-licensed authorised dealers for day-to-day exchange-control approvals; FinSurv retains jurisdiction over capital-account transactions requiring prior approval. The National Payment System Department of SARB additionally supervises clearing and settlement infrastructure under the National Payment System Act, 1998 (Act No. 78 of 1998), while the Prudential Authority and the Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) regulate banking conduct and non-bank payment service providers respectively.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The ZAR is fully convertible for current-account purposes (merchandise trade, services, dividends, interest) subject to authorised-dealer documentary verification; the capital account remains administratively controlled, meaning every cross-border capital movement must be executed through a SARB-licensed authorised dealer and non-standard structures require FinSurv pre-approval. Profit remittance by the foreign investor of ZA_PTY_LTD is treated as a current-account payment and may be paid abroad without FinSurv pre-approval once the following conditions are satisfied: (i) the 20% Dividends Tax on the gross dividend has been withheld and remitted to the South African Revenue Service (SARS); (ii) the board resolution satisfies the Companies Act 71 of 2008 solvency-and-liquidity test; (iii) the company is in good standing at the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC); and (iv) the bank has obtained a SARS tax-compliance acknowledgement plus the original inward foreign-investment declaration evidencing the non-resident shareholding. Practical hurdles: mandatory FX-dealer intermediation for every conversion; bank rejection of transactions appearing to constitute round-tripping, speculative ZAR carry-trade or unverified beneficial-ownership structures; and the administrative burden of maintaining a complete foreign-liability register. Overall assessment: current account — convertible as of right with documentary compliance; capital account — convertible with moderate administrative friction and a clean audit trail.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory timeline: the full export value of goods must be received in the Republic within 180 days from the date of shipment under Regulation 7 of the Exchange Control Regulations, 1961 and the FinSurv Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers (Export Chapter); any extension requires prior authorisation from the authorised dealer or FinSurv. Mandatory conversion: all foreign currency received for exports must be surrendered to an authorised dealer (exchanged into ZAR) unless the exporter has obtained an approved Foreign Currency Account (FCA)/retention facility; no general percentage retention allowance applies today, so the de facto requirement is 100% conversion on repatriation, with an FCA available only for approved liquidity-management purposes. Supporting documentation: SARS customs bill of entry (SAD500), commercial invoice, bill of lading or airway bill, proof of payment, and bank settlement records must be lodged with the authorised dealer. Failure to receive proceeds within the 180-day window exposes the company to SARS customs penalties, FinSurv administrative sanctions, potential blacklisting of future export facilities, and compulsory write-back of the unrecovered amount.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late penalty of ZAR20; continued non-filing for 3 years triggers administrative strike-off of the entity.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Annual Declaration (submitted with Annual Return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same timeframe as Annual Return: within 30 business days after the incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance constitutes an administrative offence; penalties up to ZAR500,000 for the company and ZAR50,000 per director for failure to disclose beneficial ownership.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) accompanied by summarised annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the company's financial year (unless jurisdictionally extended)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Estimated assessment issued where no return filed; 10% late payment penalty, 10% monthly interest compounding, and additional understatement penalties up to 200% of evaded tax.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For South African private companies, mandatory independent audit applies only when the Public Interest Score (PIS) is at least 350. PIS is calculated based on turnover, workforce size, third-party reliance, and public accountability; PIS between 100-349 requires an independent review; PIS below 100 requires no audit or review.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or IFRS for SMEs (for entities without public accountability); all financial records must be prepared and maintained in accordance with the Companies Act and applicable accounting standards.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual beneficial ownership confirmation is mandatory via CIPC. Any transfer of shares triggering beneficial ownership changes requires the Register of Beneficial Ownership to be updated within 10 business days; the updated register is filed annually with the CIPC Annual Return.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 1,500-6,000 for a low-turnover Pty Ltd if audit becomes applicable

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holidays. Small Business Corporations (SBCs) with annual turnover below ZAR 20 million qualify for progressive rates from 0% to 27%, with the first ZAR 95,750 of taxable income taxed at 0% (2024/25 rates). The general corporate rate is 27%. An additional 10% dividend withholding tax applies on distributions. No broad preferential deductions beyond standard section 11 allowances, section 12H learnership allowances, and section 12B renewable energy investment allowances. The R&D tax incentive under section 11D provides up to 150% deduction for qualifying R&D expenditure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: ITR14 Corporate Income Tax Return filed via SARS eFiling; mandatory electronic filing for all companies registered for income tax. Provisional tax returns are filed via IRP6 returns.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Provisional tax payments due within six months of the start of the year of assessment and not later than the last business day of the six-month period; second provisional payment due not later than the last business day of the year of assessment. The final annual return (ITR14) must be filed within 12 months of the end of the company's financial year. The assessment is raised by SARS based on the submitted return; the deadline is not automatically extended by payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company registration number and income tax reference number as registered with SARS.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the South African company registration number; a non-resident shareholder is not entered here. The local entity must provide its SARS tax reference code.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income: total worldwide gross income received by or accrued to the resident company, subject to specific inclusions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders do not file ITR14. The resident company reports all gross income including foreign-source trading income unless exempt.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt income: domestic dividends received by the company that are exempt under section 10(1)(k), and certain foreign dividends under section 10B.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All applicable exemptions must be claimed by the resident company; no direct non-resident filing applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before deductions: gross income less exempt income and allowable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Computed by the resident company. Non-resident shareholders have no filing obligation for this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions: allowable business expenses under section 11, including trading stock, depreciation, wear-and-tear allowances, and contributions to retirement funds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductions are claimed by the resident taxpayer. Cross-border service fees and royalties must satisfy section 23M and transfer pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income: income after all deductions, before assessed losses and tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Resident entity figure; no non-resident completion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assessed loss brought forward from prior years under section 20; limited to a maximum five-year carry-forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only available to resident companies. Losses cannot be transferred to non-resident shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Normal tax payable at 27% on taxable income, before rebates and prepayments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Strategic: for a resident company with non-resident shareholders, confirm the effective rate after any SBC concessions if turnover qualifies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits claimed under section 6quat for foreign taxes paid on foreign-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Applies only to the resident company; the company must hold evidence of foreign tax paid. Non-resident shareholders cannot claim these credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total provisional tax payments made against the assessment.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resident company reconciles its provisional payments. Non-resident shareholders do not participate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: SARS imposes a monthly penalty of up to ZAR 1,000 per month for companies failing to submit the annual return. Understatement penalties under section 223 of the Tax Administration Act 28 of 2011 range from 10% to 200% of the shortfall depending on the behavior classification (substantial understatement, intentional or negligent conduct). Interest under section 89quat of the Income Tax Act accrues at the prescribed rate (currently repo rate plus 3.5%) on unpaid tax. A 10% to 20% estimated assessment may be raised where no return is filed, and criminal prosecution can follow under section 235 of the Tax Administration Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The dividend withholding tax rate of 20% applies to cash and in-kind distributions made by a resident company to non-resident shareholders. To invoke a reduced rate under a double taxation agreement (DTA), the non-resident beneficial owner must submit a declaration (DA05) and a certificate of residence (TRC) issued by the tax authority of the treaty jurisdiction to the withholding agent before payment. The agent must retain the documentation. The DTA rate for portfolio dividend withholding is generally 5% to 15% depending on the treaty; for South Africa's principal treaties (e.g. UK, USA, Netherlands, Mauritius), rates for substantial shareholdings (at least 10% voting power) are commonly 5% or 10%. Where no declaration is submitted, the full 20% rate is withheld remitted to SARS. The procedure under the Double Taxation Agreements and the Tax Administration Act requires the TRC to be valid and to state residence of the beneficial owner. South Africa applies a participation exemption for foreign dividends but outbound dividends remain subject to the domestic withholding regime.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate on royalties (including intellectual property license fees) is 15% under section 49B of the Income Tax Act. Interest paid to non-residents is generally exempt under section 10(1)(h) if the lender is not a connected person carrying on business through a South African permanent establishment, except for interest paid to connected non-resident lenders, which is subject to 15% withholding tax under the deemed source provision. Treaty rate may be reduced to 0% for interest under most DTAs where the beneficiary is the beneficial owner, and royalties typically to 5% to 10%. The beneficial owner must submit a TRC and the relevant declaration. Where the IP is held in a low-tax jurisdiction, anti-diverted royalties rules and section 23D may impose penalties and deny deductions.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: ZAR 100 million aggregate cross-border related-party transactions per year for the requirement to prepare a Local File; ZAR 250 million for the Master File. For a company with annual turnover below ZAR 100 million and cross-border related-party transactions below ZAR 100 million, only limited contemporaneous documentation is required. SARS requires the documentation to be contemporaneous and submitted within 21 days of a request. Section 31 of the Income Tax Act empowers SARS to adjust taxable income where connected-person transacting is not at arm's length. Secondary adjustment for transfer pricing recharacterization also applies. The full Local File and Master File forms (SARS TP-1 and TP-2) are aligned with OECD BEPS Action 13 recommendations.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: South Africa does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime comparable to the UAE or Mauritius. However, the Income Tax Act incorporates the 'substance over form' doctrine, the general anti-avoidance rules (GAAR) under section 80A-L, controlled foreign company (CFC) attribution rules under section 9D, and the headquarter company regime under section 9I as economic substance tests. A company must demonstrate commercial substance, staff, operational premises, and business risks when claiming treaty benefits or headquarter company relief. SARS requires economic substance for treaty shopping protection: a conduit company with no real business purpose can be disregarded under the limitation of benefits provisions now included in the MLI and in South Africa's updated DTAs. Cross-border e-commerce retail of oversized furniture with third-party logistics providers must prove that warehousing, order processing, logistics management, and procurement functions are actually performed in South Africa to avoid CFC attribution and GAAR challenges.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting e-commerce gross receipts, understating online furniture sales, using personal bank accounts for business deposits, or falsifying VAT/income tax records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction under the Tax Administration Act section 234 and the Income Tax Act: imprisonment up to 5 years, and a fine of up to ZAR 30,000 per charge. SARS may impose a 200% understatement penalty under section 223, plus daily interest at the prescribed rate. Assets and bank accounts may be seized through civil judgment. In addition, a 20% VAT penalty and additional VAT and penalties apply under the Value-Added Tax Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and members of the board are jointly and severally liable for the company's tax debts under section 18 of the Tax Administration Act if the company failed to pay employee taxes (PAYE), VAT, or withholding taxes. For general corporate income tax debts, the personal liability regime requires proof that the director knowingly assisted in the evasion, was negligent, or authorized the conduct, allowing SARS to pierce the corporate veil under common law and section 20 of the Companies Act 71 of 2008. Severe cases trigger orders for civil restitution, freezing of personal assets, travel bans under the Prevention of Corruption Act and the Extradition Act, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Incorporating a South African holding company that obtains dividend or interest treaty relief without any physical office, employees, bank account management, or substantive decision-making in South Africa; using the South African entity as a pure pass-through for offshore e-commerce profit shifting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The general anti-avoidance rules under sections 80A-L allow SARS to disregard the transaction, recharacterize the structure, deny treaty benefits, and impose a 200% understatement penalty. The CFC rules under section 9D attribute undistributed profits to South African residents. The courts have confirmed in cases such as STC v Colonial and SARS v NWK Ltd (though NWK was later qualified by SARS) that transactions without commercial substance are invalid. Administrative penalties of up to ZAR 5 million may apply for failure to file TP documentation. SARS may also invoke the limitation of benefits clause and deny all treaty relief. The Financial Intelligence Centre Act (FICA) exposes the entity to monetary penalties for inaccurate beneficial ownership records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be held personally liable for the tax liability if the company was used as a facade or vehicle for the evasion or for improper profit diversion. Under the Companies Act, a director who knowingly carries on business recklessly, with gross negligence, or for a fraudulent purpose is liable for the company's debts. Personal restraint orders, asset seizure orders, and travel bans may be imposed; directors may additionally be banned from serving as directors for up to 10 years under section 162 of the Companies Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Mis-pricing cross-border transactions with a connected foreign logistics company or IP holding entity, artificially reducing South African taxable profit by inflating logistics fees, overpaying management fees, or shifting profit through royalty payments without documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SARS may adjust the taxable income to reflect an arm's length price under section 31, leading to additional tax of up to 27% (or 28% for years before FY2023) plus interest. An understatement penalty under section 223 of the Tax Administration Act of 50% to 200% applies for the substantial understatement. Where the transaction is found to have a mainly tax avoidance purpose, the GAAR penalties apply. Secondary transfer pricing adjustment may result in a deemed loan and dividend withholding tax (DWT) at 20% on the notional dividend where the secondary adjustment is treated as a distribution. Criminal prosecution applies where false documentation is submitted, with penalties of up to ZAR 25,000 or imprisonment of up to 3 years per false statement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign off on falsified transfer pricing file, or who cause the company to provide false information to SARS, incur personal liability under section 234 and section 235 of the Tax Administration Act. They are subject to civil restitution for taxes owed, punitive damages, travel bans, and imprisonment up to 5 years. Where the transfer pricing manipulation forms part of money laundering, the Prevention of Organised Crime Act allows SARS and the National Prosecuting Authority to seize personal assets and freeze bank accounts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using a South African (Pty) Ltd engaged in online furniture sales to conceal the proceeds of fraud, third-party payment processors (Stripe, BNPL platforms) being used as laundering channels, accepting proceeds from illegal sources, or failing to register as an accountable institution under FICA where advances loans or provides payment services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001, as amended by the General Laws Amendment Act 2022, prescribes administrative penalties up to ZAR 50 million for accountable institutions. Criminal sanctions include fines up to ZAR 100 million and imprisonment up to 30 years. The Prevention of Organised Crime Act 121 of 1998 provides for asset forfeiture and proceeds of crime recovery without conviction. Contempt due to failure to file beneficial ownership returns under the Companies Act can result in a fine of up to ZAR 500,000 and imprisonment up to 3 months.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors constitute part of management; a director who knowingly conducts business with proceeds of unlawful activity commits a statutory offence and is liable to imprisonment up to 15 years. Directors may face personal asset forfeiture, curatorship orders over their property, and travel bans of indefinite duration. Directors who knowingly failed to prevent money laundering while holding supervisory responsibility are personally liable under section 42 of FICA.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold Dividend or Non-Resident Taxes
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Declaring and paying dividends to non-resident shareholders without withholding the 20% dividend withholding tax; failing to withhold 15% interest/royalty withholding tax on connected non-resident lenders or IP owners; failure to submit the DTA declaration forms.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding agent is jointly and severally liable for the tax. The penalty is 20% (DWT) of the dividend amount plus interest from the date the dividend was paid. For royalties or interest, the tax authority imposes the 15% tax plus understatement penalties up to 200% and interest at the prescribed rate. Criminal prosecution may follow under section 235 of the Tax Administration Act for deliberate failure, leading to imprisonment of up to 2 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorise a dividend declaration knowing that withholding tax has not been paid and who are personally vested with the responsibility to make payments on behalf of the company are jointly and severally liable. SARS may assess directors directly under section 18 of the Tax Administration Act; the liability extends to unpaid withholding taxes, interest, and penalties. Directors' personal assets may be attached under a tax judgment; travel bans may be issued where outstanding tax exceeds ZAR 50,000.
